key_insight: An integrated deep-learning and fuzzy-control method aims to adapt robotic GMAW parameters to changing weld-seam conditions while optimizing weld quality.
engineering_relevance: The approach targets reduced manual reprogramming and more consistent robotic welding when joint geometry, assembly conditions, or heat input vary.
method: Combine quality-grade-oriented process planning with site-specific multi-objective parameter optimization.
Use semi-supervised semantic segmentation to perceive seams and molten pools, alongside neural weld-formation prediction for spatter suppression.
Apply fuzzy adaptive control to adjust the welding process.
evidence_signal: Experiments used Q235 carbon-steel butt joints and developed a response-surface model linking current, travel speed, torch angle, and nozzle height to weld geometry; the abstract reports no quantitative performance gains.
watch_item: Transferability beyond Q235 butt joints and robustness under production conditions require further validation.
paper_title: Deep Learning-Based Welding Process Optimization and Adaptive Control Method for Welding Robots
